scope: Selected Canvas Pages offline reading packet: source identity, inert HTML retention, exclusive complete publication; no edits or duplicate execution.
decision: No blocker found in the two exact product sources reviewed. Final native HTTP-to-CLI process and current composition receipts remain separate receiving gates.
checks: Course ID, requested URL or explicit page_id, returned normalized page IDs and provider identity are bound before rendering; alias duplicates are refused.
Current official Pages API URL-first numeric locator semantics match the implemented parser and encoded request path.
Original UTF-8 HTML is retained as escaped inert source, including carriage-return handling; the reading projection is separately labelled and escaped.
Provider HTML cannot introduce active DOM resources; generated links use the verified Canvas source and fixed encoded course/page paths.
All selected pages are collected within declared source and output limits before publication. This is honestly described as sequential reads, not an atomic backup.
Temporary complete bytes are written, flushed, fsynced and closed before exclusive hard-link publication. No overwrite fallback is used.
Existing files, directories and dangling symlinks are refused before transport; a destination raced into existence is protected by exclusive publication.
Failure before publication cleans the private temporary best-effort; cleanup failure after publication is a warning on successful committed output.
limits: Source review only; no live Canvas account/provider calls, no author source edits, no repeated module suite.
The acceptance does not assert cross-filesystem publication support or directory-fsync power-loss durability.
Projection fidelity for arbitrary malformed HTML is not a backup claim; exact escaped source remains available.
receipt_location_note: Preserved on Mac after a hash-only receipt-write SSH connection to the ThinkPad timed out before reaching the host. Acceptance is tied to exact source bytes independently read earlier; no latest-head assertion.
